note: PROVISIONAL. Unlike rollback_completion_bounds.json, these values are enforced: the core compiles the same numbers in (IngressLimits::DECLARED in rust/azazel-edge-core/src/ingress.rs) and a core unit test fails if the two differ. The core does not read this file at run time. Not hardware evidence, and not a program-plan section 8 target: those are unchanged.

quotas.excess_policy: Lines beyond the rate or the per-poll bound stay unread in the EVE file and are read on later polls. Past backlog_bound_bytes of unread file, flow records are shed, then dns, stats and every other non-alert type at each further multiple of the bound. Alerts are never shed; past alert_backlog_bound_bytes an ingress_alert_backlog summary is recorded and alerts keep being read at the declared rate. Shed counts leave the core as at most one ingress_shed summary per audit interval in ingress-audit.jsonl beside the normalized event log.

basis.method: release build of azazel-edge-core on main at 4b5242c (decision path unchanged by OF-06; the old reader had no bound), Edge defaults, enforcement off, AI forward off, stdout off, normalized log on: 200000 pre-written synthetic EVE alerts (the SO-04 harness's eve_flood line shape, about 300 bytes each) read from the start of the file, time until all 200000 decisions were in the normalized log; docker on colima, aarch64 (image edge414-ci:py311)
basis.margin_rule: less than half the minimum observed sustained decision rate, rounded down to the next 500 lines/s; at or above the SO-04 harness's eve_flood rate (2000 EVE alerts/s) so SO-04 runs are not throttled by the quota
basis.per_poll_rule: admit_per_poll is 0.6 s of the quota, so the token bucket is not the limit while one poll's work plus the 200 ms poll interval stays under 0.6 s; examine_per_poll is four times admit_per_poll
basis.backlog_rule: backlog_bound_bytes (8 MiB) is several seconds of the quota at real EVE line sizes; alert_backlog_bound_bytes (256 MiB) is a hard record point, not a drop point
basis.so04_check: SO-04 harness re-run twice on the OF-06 tree (eve_flood 2000 alerts/s, below the quota): start max 2408.7 and 1415.7 ms (bound 5000 ms), completion max 1773.6 and 1592.9 ms over all action types (provisional bounds 5000 ms), 0 violations, 150/150 samples per part in both runs.
basis.contended_check: Re-measured the same way the same day while other containers ran on the same 2-CPU colima VM (main binary, 60000-line backlog, decisions over 8 s): 5252, 3348 and 3957 lines/s. All exceed the quota. Under that contention the OF-06 core admitted 2263-2493 lines/s against its 2500 lines/s token bucket: the quota is a ceiling, not a promise.
